# dsh-visual
Interactive cards inside a DeepSeek Harness conversation. The model publishes a self-contained HTML
card (or a draggable flowchart), the tool **blocks until the user submits**, and the user's click, c
omments, form fields and card state come back as the tool result.
No assistant text, no chat message, no artifact preview — a real card in the message stream.
## Features
- **Blocking, not fire-and-forget.** `visual` stays pending until the user submits, so the answer ar

rives as the tool result and the agent continues in the same turn.
- **Scriptable cards.** Inline `<
script>` runs per card through a small bridge (`dshVisual.root`, `dshVisual.setState`), so cards can

toggle, validate and prefill themselves.
- **Structured answers.** Buttons (`data-visual-action`),

inputs (`data-visual-field`), comments and card state are merged into one JSON answer.
- **Comments
with pins.** Right-click any element to leave a comment; the answer carries the element's selector a

nd label so the model knows exactly what each note is about.
- **Flow editor.** Pass a `flow` graph
instead of HTML: drag nodes, double-click to rename, connect, delete, then hand the edited graph bac

k.
- **Parallel safe.** Several cards in one turn each get their own bridge and state; nothing leaks

between them.
- **Cancellable and time-bounded.** `timeoutMs` and a stop button turn the card read-
only instead of hanging forever.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness 0.1.0-rc.1 and newer, below 0.3 (prerelease builds included)
- Node.js 20 or newe

## Parameters
| Parameter | Type | Description |

| `title` | string | Card header title. |
| `html` | string | Complete, self-contained HTML document

. Styles are scoped; scripts run per card. |
| `flow` | object | Flow graph `{nodes, edges}` rendere

d as an editable canvas instead of HTML. |
| `data` | object | Initial state exposed as `dshVisual.d

ata` to the card script. |
| `height` | number | Initial card height in px (160–900). The card can r

esize itself. |
| `actions` | array | Action registry `{id, label}` for the footer chips and button

labels. |
| `timeoutMs` | number | How long to wait for a submit (default 10 min, max 1 h). |
Every field is optional except one of `html` or `flow`.
## Card protocol
### Buttons and fields
- `data-visual-action="id"` — clicking submits that action together with the fields, state and comme

nts.
- `data-visual-field="name"` — read from the card on submit and returned under `answer.payload.

fields`.
- The footer always shows a neutral **交还** button (`answer.action = "done"`). It never impl
ies approval: review cards should carry an explicit approve/revise action of their own.
### Scripts and state
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Each card is compiled as `new Function('dshVisual', source)(bridge)`, so parallel cards cannot see e
led as `new Function('dshVisual', source)(bridge)`, so parallel cards cannot see each other's state.
### Comments
Right-click any element inside the card, type a note, and it is pinned with a number. The answer car
ries them in `answer.comments` as `{ selector, label, text }`.
### Timeout and cancel
When `timeoutMs` elapses the call returns `action: "timeout"`; stopping the turn returns `action: "c
ancelled"`. In both cases the card becomes read-only and its footer explains why.
## Development

## Releasing
Publishing is automatic: pushing a `v*` tag runs the release workflow, which verifies `npm run check
`, publishes to npm with provenance, and opens a GitHub Release.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Publishing uses npm trusted publishing: the workflow exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for a short-liv
ed npm credential, so no `NPM_TOKEN` secret is stored. Configure it once under the package's **Setti
ngs → Trusted publishing** on npmjs.com (owner `MjxUpUp`, repository `dsh-visual`, workflow `publish
rusted publishing** on npmjs.com (owner `MjxUpUp`, repository `dsh-visual`, workflow `publish.yml`).
